findings.issue_text: Fabricated zod construct: dynamic catch-all keys via z.string().toString() evaluate to '[object Object]', so both computed keys collapse to the same literal key and no wildcard matching exists in zod objects
Unknown properties in the token response are stripped by zod rather than passed through, so expiry fields are silently dropped from every refreshed token persisted to credential.key
The inferred schema type has no refresh_token field, making refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token (line 23) a TS type error that breaks the build

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data?, error?}) instead of the parsed data, breaking callers like CalendarService.ts:93-95 that treat the return value as the parsed credentials when updating prisma.credential

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-7 - z.string().toString() evaluates to literal '[object String]', so both computed keys are identical constants and the second overwrites the first; combined with z.object's strip behavior the schema only validates access_token and strips expiry_date, so token responses with no expiry pass validation and callers store undefined expiry_date

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16-19 - In partial configuration (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED true but CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT unset), the sync branch strips the real refresh_token/expiry_date and replaces the genuine refresh token with the placeholder 'refresh_token', which is then persisted, permanently destroying the credential and requiring re-auth

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11-15 - No defined return contract: sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while fallback returns axios responses (e.g., zoho-bigin/zohocrm), so axios-based callers accessing tokenInfo.data.error get undefined and throw TypeError, breaking token refresh for zoho-bigin and zohocrm when credential sharing is enabled

app-credential.ts:64-69 - Endpoint never validates the decrypted keys payload against the app's credential schema (e.g., googleCredentialSchema), so malformed sync payloads are persisted verbatim into credential.key, and there is no error handling for symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse failures causing unhandled 500s

salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-95 - Salesforce uses a hand-rolled unconditional fetch to the Salesforce token endpoint with no expiry check and no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED guard, causing unnecessary token endpoint calls for all users and excluding Salesforce from the credential sync architecture

app-credential.ts:22-93 - Sync protocol has no deletion/revocation path: when an app is disconnected on the parent instance, the self-hosted instance is never told to remove the Credential row, leaving orphaned credentials

zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:85-95 - Wrong identifier passed as sync user key: refreshOAuthTokens is called with the credential's row ID (credentialId) instead of the Cal.com user ID, so parent-side lookup can never resolve it and zoho-bigin token sync can never succeed

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw safeParse result object, and CalendarService.ts in googlecalendar persists it directly to credential.key, corrupting the stored credentials with a wrapper object ({success, data, error}) instead of parsed data and breaking Google Calendar for all self-hosted users on first token refresh

The 'minimum token response' schema uses [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), which produces a literal object key that can never match a real response property; the schema effectively enforces only access_token and never validates the presence of expiry_date

salesforce CalendarService adds an unconditional token-refresh implementation with no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate, adding a network roundtrip and DB write on every service instantiation, and its statusText !== 'OK' check falsely throws HttpError 400 when statusText is empty despite 2xx status (HTTP/2, proxies)

The credential-sync fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication (no shared secret or signature), making it impossible for the receiving endpoint to authenticate the caller and allowing anyone who discovers the URL to retrieve credentials for any calcomUserId

refreshOAuthTokens.ts is typed loosely (refreshFunction: () => any) and returns either a fetch Response or provider-specific data; zoho-bigin, zohocrm, and hubspot callers assume an axios-style response (accessing tokenInfo.data.error), causing a TypeError on every refresh when credential sharing is enabled

office365calendar CalendarService deletes the console.error diagnostics and tolerate-and-continue behavior on token-parse failure; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on any schema mismatch, hard-failing mid-booking where old credentials previously kept working

parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates a literal placeholder 'refresh_token' string when the parsed response lacks refresh_token, and callers persist it into credential.key, overwriting real refresh tokens and permanently bricking the credential if the sync endpoint is later removed

zoho-bigin/api/add.ts hardcodes '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback' instead of deriving it from appConfig.slug, removing the single source of truth and risking an OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch if the app slug changes

The webhook receiver accepts credential pushes for any appSlug, but consume-side sync is wired into only 8 apps; for other OAuth apps the two credential stores silently diverge with nondeterministic expiry outcomes

.env.example instructions are self-contradictory: they require a 32-byte key for AES256 but recommend 'openssl rand -base64 24', which produces a 24-byte key, leading to potential key-length failures or ambiguous entropy depending on how symmetricDecrypt interprets the key

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper in the non-shared path, which is persisted as the credential key, corrupting stored credentials so credential.key.access_token resolves to undefined after the first refresh

Zod schema uses [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to the literal key '[object Object]' (declared twice, second overwriting first) and strips expiry_date/expires_in fields, so expiry data is silently dropped from persisted tokens

refreshOAuthTokens sync path returns a raw fetch Response while Google, Hubspot, zoho-bigin, and zohocrm call sites expect a parsed body/axios shape, so undefined tokens are persisted and errors are treated as success

app-credential webhook handler uses a findFirst-then-create check-then-insert pattern with no unique (userId, appId) constraint, allowing concurrent requests to create duplicate Credential rows and subsequent updates to pick an arbitrary one
The webhook handler's findFirst lookup only filters by userId and appId, ignoring teamId, so team-scoped and personal credentials are indistinguishable and the wrong credential may be updated
The refreshOAuthTokens sync endpoint call has no auth header, timeout, response.ok check, or circuit breaker, so a degraded sync endpoint cascades into a full calendar-sync outage

Salesforce bypasses the shared refreshOAuthTokens abstraction with its own unconditional fetch, so credential-sharing mode doesn't apply, and the refresh now runs eagerly on every getInstance() instead of lazily on 401

Salesforce CalendarService contains an unreachable `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure, leaving duplicate error strings that will diverge on edit

zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects a user id, so with sharing enabled the sync endpoint is queried with the wrong identifier and the shared-credential path never works for zoho-bigin

parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal sentinel string 'refresh_token' when no refresh token is present, and call sites persist it, so local refresh fallback later sends the fake token to providers and permanently breaks reconnection

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string|undefined expression rather than a boolean, and its effective meaning differs between the webhook handler (flag only) and refreshOAuthTokens (flag plus endpoint requirement)

The refreshOAuthTokens/parseRefreshTokenResponse abstraction cannot represent the incompatible response shapes of seven providers; the design should be replaced with a single normalized {access_token, expires_at} return type with sync fetch, status check, and sentinel handling centralized

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result object instead of parsed data; Google Calendar stores the wrapper as credential key, breaking credential.key for all users regardless of feature flag

refreshOAuthTokens returns inconsistent shapes across branches (fetch Response in sync mode vs google-auth response); Google call site assumes old {res} contract, so token refresh crashes with TypeError in sync mode

parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses z.string().toString() computed keys that both evaluate to '[object Object]'; the second key overwrites the first and no expiry is ever captured, silently stripping expiry_date/expires_in in sync mode

Fabricated refresh_token = 'refresh_token' placeholder is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and is persisted by callers (office365calendar, zoomvideo), overwriting real refresh tokens when Microsoft omits refresh_token, permanently breaking the credential

Zoho (zoho-bigin and zohocrm) call sites read tokenInfo.data.error per axios contract but sync mode returns a fetch Response whose .data is undefined, so errors are treated as success and empty/garbage tokens are persisted
Hubspot assigns sync-mode fetch Response to a HubspotToken-typed variable; downstream expiresIn read yields undefined/NaN, persisting invalid expiry and breaking HubSpot sync mode

Salesforce CalendarService added an unconditional token refresh plus prisma.credential.update on every service construction, not gated by the feature flag, causing token-endpoint hammering and needless credential churn for all users
office365calendar deleted the zod-failure error logging (console.error for 'Outlook error grabbing new tokens') with no replacement, making parse failures silent and removing observability

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is a no-op: z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate to '[object Object]', so the second computed key overwrites the first and any response object passes validation

CalendarService.ts stores the SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as credential.key instead of the parsed .data, overwriting Google Calendar credentials with invalid wrapper data on every token refresh
Salesforce CalendarService uses .data correctly, but in sharing-enabled mode .data is a stripped empty object, wiping instance_url and access_token
Webhook secret in app-credential.ts compared with plain !== instead of a constant-time comparison, allowing a timing oracle to recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
app-credential.ts endpoint authorizes overwriting any user's OAuth credentials based solely on possession of a single static secret, with no per-user scoping, key shape validation, or rate limiting

Zoho Bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing the sync endpoint to return and persist another user's tokens (cross-tenant credential bleed)

New logic has zero test coverage: refreshOAuthTokens.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the sync branch in salesforce CalendarService.ts (~lines 75-95), and the entire apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts have no corresponding test changes
office365calendar CalendarService.ts removes console.error zod-error diagnostics and now throws via parseRefreshTokenResponse on schema failure, whereas previously it logged and continued

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) which Google's CalendarService.ts (~line 96) stores verbatim into prisma.credential.update({data: {key}}) instead of the parsed data as before
Security posture of the new webhook endpoint: header comparison and unauthenticated shape of req.body need review
Suspicious schema construction in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: [z.string().toString()] used as a computed key does not implement the intended 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of .data, and Google CalendarService persists it directly, so every Google token refresh rewrites Credential.key to a Zod envelope without access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, silently corrupting all Google Calendar credentials

parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites missing refresh tokens with the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token' with no dual-write or backfill, causing irreversible loss of real refresh tokens for all synced users if credential sharing is disabled or the sync endpoint fails

Salesforce CalendarService persists the parsed key using minimumTokenResponseSchema when credential sharing is enabled, which strips instance_url, id, and signature from Credential.key, breaking jsforce connections with no restore path except re-auth
Salesforce CalendarService performs a token fetch+update on every service instantiation (constructor path) rather than only on 401 recovery, multiplying opportunities to overwrite stored credentials

Hubspot, Zoho-Bigin, and ZohoCRM CalendarService treat refreshOAuthTokens' raw fetch Response as an axios-style result, reading .access_token or .data on an object with no such properties, so downstream prisma.credential.update writes undefined/garbage over valid credentials

The app-credential sync endpoint performs a blind full-object overwrite of Credential.key with no export/backup of the prior value and no dual-write, destroying the user's only working credential copy if the sync payload is bad
symmetricDecrypt in app-credential.ts is called with process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '' instead of failing closed on a missing encryption key

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook body schema only supports `{ userId, appSlug, keys }` and the handler logic only performs `credential.update` or `credential.create` based on existence. There is no request shape or code path to delete/revoke an existing credential (e.g., no `action`/`deleted` flag, no `prisma.credential.delete`). adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'minimum token response' schema uses [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), which produces a literal object key that can never match a real response property; the schema effectively enforces only access_token and never validates the presence of expiry_date

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is declared as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In JS/TS, computed property names like `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate immediately to a single literal string key (whatever `toString()` returns), not a “match any string key” pattern. So this schema does not validate “any numeric expiry field” from real token responses (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`), and effectively only guarantees `access_token` (plus potentially an impossible/literal key). The finding correctly identifies a real correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code issues a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and does not include any authentication material (no shared secret header, signature, token, etc.). This is directly verifiable from the diff. While the exact impact depends on how that external endpoint is implemented, the finding’s core point—that the request provides no way for the receiving endpoint to authenticate the caller based on this request alone—is a real issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts is typed loosely (refreshFunction: () => any) and returns either a fetch Response or provider-specific data; zoho-bigin, zohocrm, and hubspot callers assume an axios-style response (accessing tokenInfo.data.error), causing a TypeError on every refresh when credential sharing is enabled

office365calendar CalendarService deletes the console.error diagnostics and tolerate-and-continue behavior on token-parse failure; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on any schema mismatch, hard-failing mid-booking where old credentials previously kept working

The finding’s core claim (loss of diagnostics + new hard-fail behavior) is directly verifiable in the diff, though the “mid-booking where old credentials previously kept working” part is contextual/speculative beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .env.example instructions are self-contradictory: they require a 32-byte key for AES256 but recommend 'openssl rand -base64 24', which produces a 24-byte key, leading to potential key-length failures or ambiguous entropy depending on how symmetricDecrypt interprets the key

adjudication.rationale: The added .env.example comments for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY state the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but then recommend generating it via `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes (encoded to a longer base64 string). This is internally inconsistent in the diff itself and could mislead deployers into using a key length different from what the comment requires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper in the non-shared path, which is persisted as the credential key, corrupting stored credentials so credential.key.access_token resolves to undefined after the first refresh

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the entire `safeParse` result object (`SafeParseReturnType`) rather than the parsed data (`.data`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, this return value is assigned to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That means the DB will store an object like `{ success: true, data: {...} }` instead of the expected credential payload, so later code accessing `credential.key.access_token` would indeed be `undefined` (it would be under `credential.key.data.access_token`). This is a concrete, diff-verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema uses [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to the literal key '[object Object]' (declared twice, second overwriting first) and strips expiry_date/expires_in fields, so expiry data is silently dropped from persisted tokens

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is declared as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(), })`. In JS, `z.string()` is an object, so `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal string `"[object Object]"`. That means the schema is actually defining properties named `"[object Object]"` (twice), not an index signature / pattern for arbitrary numeric expiry fields. As a result, when credential sharing is enabled, `safeParse(response)` will almost always fail because typical token responses contain keys like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, not `"[object Object]"`, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`. The proposed finding’s core issue about the computed key being wrong is verifiable in the diff; the specific claim about “silently dropped” expiry is less accurate than “parsing fails/throws”, but the defect is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens sync path returns a raw fetch Response while Google, Hubspot, zoho-bigin, and zohocrm call sites expect a parsed body/axios shape, so undefined tokens are persisted and errors are treated as success
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: in the credential-sync (sharing enabled) path the helper returns a raw `fetch` Response, while multiple integration refresh callers (e.g., Google/Hubspot and others) expect an axios-like `res.data` or an integration-specific token object. This mismatch leads to undefined/incorrect token handling and runtime errors unless return type or call sites are adjusted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook handler uses a findFirst-then-create check-then-insert pattern with no unique (userId, appId) constraint, allowing concurrent requests to create duplicate Credential rows and subsequent updates to pick an arbitrary one

adjudication.rationale: The new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler does use a non-atomic `findFirst` سپس `create` pattern (`prisma.credential.findFirst` then `prisma.credential.create`). However, the finding’s key claim—“with no unique (userId, appId) constraint, allowing concurrent requests to create duplicate rows”—is not verifiable from this diff because the Prisma schema / DB constraints are not shown. If a unique constraint exists, concurrent creates would fail with a uniqueness error rather than create duplicates. So the duplicate-row conclusion depends on information not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler's findFirst lookup only filters by userId and appId, ignoring teamId, so team-scoped and personal credentials are indistinguishable and the wrong credential may be updated

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the credential lookup is explicitly scoped to `userId` (`where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`). Team-scoped credentials would typically not match this filter if they are stored with `teamId` and a null/absent `userId` (which is consistent with other diff context: `refreshOAuthTokens` only triggers syncing when `credential.userId` is truthy, implying team credentials likely have `userId` null). The webhook request body also contains only `userId` (no `teamId`), suggesting it is intentionally designed to sync user credentials only. Therefore the claim that team-scoped and personal credentials are “indistinguishable” and that the wrong one may be updated is not directly supported/verified by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The refreshOAuthTokens sync endpoint call has no auth header, timeout, response.ok check, or circuit breaker, so a degraded sync endpoint cascades into a full calendar-sync outage

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when syncing is enabled it calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no authentication/secret header, no timeout/abort handling, and it returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok`. Call sites then proceed as if a valid token response will be available, so a slow/down/non-2xx sync endpoint can block or fail token refresh and thereby break integrations that depend on refreshed OAuth tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal sentinel string 'refresh_token' when no refresh token is present, and call sites persist it, so local refresh fallback later sends the fake token to providers and permanently breaks reconnection
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse inserts the literal string 'refresh_token' when the response lacks a refresh token, and that fake value gets persisted and later used, breaking refresh/reconnection. This matches the golden issue about hardcoding 'refresh_token' and causing authentication failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string|undefined expression rather than a boolean, and its effective meaning differs between the webhook handler (flag only) and refreshOAuthTokens (flag plus endpoint requirement)

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` being imported from `@calcom/lib/constants` and used in boolean contexts (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`, `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)`). Nothing in the diff indicates it is a `string | undefined`; that part of the finding depends on code outside the diff and is not verifiable here. While it is true that the webhook handler gates only on the flag, whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and `userId`, the diff does not establish this as a defect—those conditions appear intentional (webhook receiving pushed credentials vs. optional sync endpoint for refresh).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The refreshOAuthTokens/parseRefreshTokenResponse abstraction cannot represent the incompatible response shapes of seven providers; the design should be replaced with a single normalized {access_token, expires_at} return type with sync fetch, status check, and sentinel handling centralized

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` sometimes returns a native `fetch` `Response` (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` + `userId`) and otherwise returns whatever the provider refresh function returns. Call sites assume incompatible shapes: e.g. Google Calendar now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` which works for the Google auth library response (gaxios with `.data`) but will be a `Response` without `.data` when the sync endpoint path is taken, causing `token` to be `undefined` and subsequent `token.access_token` access to fail. HubSpot similarly assumes the returned value is a `HubspotToken`, but the sync path returns a `Response`. This demonstrates the abstraction does not normalize/centralize response handling and cannot safely cover different provider response types as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result object instead of parsed data; Google Calendar stores the wrapper as credential key, breaking credential.key for all users regardless of feature flag

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`/`minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` (a Zod SafeParse result with `{ success, data|error }`), not the parsed `data` object. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, this return value is assigned to `key` and written to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, whereas previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the actual credential payload object. This will store the safeParse wrapper object as the credential key, breaking expected `credential.key` shape. Also, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` is called unconditionally in the Google Calendar refresh path, so the bug applies regardless of the feature flag/endpoint (the flag only changes which schema is used, not the return type).

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns inconsistent shapes across branches (fetch Response in sync mode vs google-auth response); Google call site assumes old {res} contract, so token refresh crashes with TypeError in sync mode
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root problem: refreshOAuthTokens returns different response shapes depending on the sync/fetch path vs the google-auth path. In sync mode it returns a fetch Response without `.data`, but the caller expects the old `{res}`/`.data` structure, leading to `undefined` and a runtime TypeError when accessing `access_token`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses z.string().toString() computed keys that both evaluate to '[object Object]'; the second key overwrites the first and no expiry is ever captured, silently stripping expiry_date/expires_in in sync mode

Fabricated refresh_token = 'refresh_token' placeholder is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and is persisted by callers (office365calendar, zoomvideo), overwriting real refresh tokens when Microsoft omits refresh_token, permanently breaking the credential

Zoho (zoho-bigin and zohocrm) call sites read tokenInfo.data.error per axios contract but sync mode returns a fetch Response whose .data is undefined, so errors are treated as success and empty/garbage tokens are persisted

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding specifically claims Zoho (zoho-bigin and zohocrm) call sites expect an axios-style response (`tokenInfo.data.error`) but in sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` (no `.data`), causing errors/tokens to be mishandled. While the diff *does* introduce a similar response-shape mismatch risk for other integrations (e.g., Google code still does `res?.data` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens`, which would be wrong if it returns a `fetch` Response), the stated Zoho issue itself is not evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hubspot assigns sync-mode fetch Response to a HubspotToken-typed variable; downstream expiresIn read yields undefined/NaN, persisting invalid expiry and breaking HubSpot sync mode

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken` is typed as `HubspotToken` but is now assigned the return value of `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` performs a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), not parsed JSON. The Hubspot refresh logic immediately proceeds as if it received a token payload (comment indicates it computes expiry from the token), so properties like `expiresIn`/`expires_in` will be `undefined`, leading to invalid expiry calculations (e.g., `NaN`) or runtime errors and breaking HubSpot sync mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService added an unconditional token refresh plus prisma.credential.update on every service construction, not gated by the feature flag, causing token-endpoint hammering and needless credential churn for all users

adjudication.rationale: The diff chunk for `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` only shows new imports (`zod`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) and a new `salesforceTokenSchema` definition. It does not show any new unconditional token refresh logic, any call to a token endpoint, or any `prisma.credential.update` added during service construction. Since the alleged behavior is not present (or at least not visible/verifiable) in the provided diff, the finding is not substantiated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar deleted the zod-failure error logging (console.error for 'Outlook error grabbing new tokens') with no replacement, making parse failures silent and removing observability

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens...", ...)` block after `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` is indeed removed. However, it is replaced by `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, and that helper explicitly `throw`s when the parse fails (`throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")`). Therefore parse failures are not “silent” in this diff; they now fail fast via an exception (though with less detailed, provider-specific logging). The finding’s core claim that failures become silent is a misread, so it’s not a clear defect based solely on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is a no-op: z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate to '[object Object]', so the second computed key overwrites the first and any response object passes validation

adjudication.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions call `toString()` on Zod schema objects, which results in the same string key (typically "[object Object]") rather than a dynamic/index signature. The second entry overwrites the first, so the intended "any numeric expiry field" constraint is not enforced. The resulting schema effectively only requires `access_token` and ignores/strips other fields, meaning many invalid token responses (e.g., missing expiry/refresh_token) will still validate under this branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts stores the SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as credential.key instead of the parsed .data, overwriting Google Calendar credentials with invalid wrapper data on every token refresh

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *SafeParseReturnType* object from `schema.safeParse(...)` (it returns `refreshTokenResponse`, not `refreshTokenResponse.data`). But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That means the DB `credential.key` will be overwritten with the wrapper `{ success: true, data: ... }` (and possibly other fields), not the actual credential payload. This is a concrete mismatch introduced in the diff and would corrupt stored Google Calendar credentials on refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService uses .data correctly, but in sharing-enabled mode .data is a stripped empty object, wiping instance_url and access_token

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show Salesforce CalendarService reading a token response via a `.data` property in “sharing-enabled mode”, nor does it show any logic that would replace token data with an empty object. The only new sharing-related parsing utility (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`) is added and used in Google/Office365 code paths, and it does not “strip” responses to an empty object; it safeParses and (if missing) injects a placeholder `refresh_token`. The Salesforce file snippet only shows new imports and a new `salesforceTokenSchema` definition, without any refresh/parse/update logic changes that match the described issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret in app-credential.ts compared with plain !== instead of a constant-time comparison, allowing a timing oracle to recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler validates the webhook secret via a direct inequality check: `req.headers[... ] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is a normal JavaScript string/primitive comparison, which is not guaranteed to be constant-time and may short-circuit based on mismatch position/length. Since this is used to gate access to a privileged webhook endpoint, it is a legitimate security concern to use a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to avoid potential timing side-channels.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts endpoint authorizes overwriting any user's OAuth credentials based solely on possession of a single static secret, with no per-user scoping, key shape validation, or rate limiting

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the only authorization check is a shared static secret comparison (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` vs `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). After that, the handler trusts `req.body.userId` and `req.body.appSlug` and will `update`/`create` a `credential` record for that user/app. There is no additional scoping tying the caller to a specific user, no validation of the decrypted `keys` structure beyond `JSON.parse(...)`, and no rate limiting/throttling logic in the endpoint. So possession of the one secret is sufficient to overwrite any user's stored OAuth credential payload by choosing any `userId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing the sync endpoint to return and persist another user's tokens (cross-tenant credential bleed)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not include any Zoho Bigin CalendarService code or any refreshOAuthTokens call sites for Zoho Bigin. All visible usages of refreshOAuthTokens in the diff (Google Calendar, Hubspot, Lark, Office365 Calendar, Office365 Video) pass `credential.userId` (or equivalent), and there is no instance shown where a `credentialId` is passed instead. Therefore the claimed cross-tenant token bleed issue is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New logic has zero test coverage: refreshOAuthTokens.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the sync branch in salesforce CalendarService.ts (~lines 75-95), and the entire apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts have no corresponding test changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds new runtime code (new webhook endpoint and new OAuth refresh helpers) without showing any accompanying test-file changes. However, the claim of “zero test coverage” is not verifiable from this diff alone because existing tests (not modified here) could already exercise these paths, and lack of new/updated tests is a quality/process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService.ts removes console.error zod-error diagnostics and now throws via parseRefreshTokenResponse on schema failure, whereas previously it logged and continued

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code changes from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` plus a `console.error(...)` on failure (and then continuing) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws when `safeParse` fails and removes the prior detailed `console.error` logging. That behavioral change is real, but it’s not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by the diff—throwing on invalid token responses can be the more correct behavior than logging and continuing with stale credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) which Google's CalendarService.ts (~line 96) stores verbatim into prisma.credential.update({data: {key}}) instead of the parsed data as before

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)` (a Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data` itself. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code was changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed credential object) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then passes that value directly as `key` into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That means Prisma will store the wrapper object instead of the credential payload, which is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Security posture of the new webhook endpoint: header comparison and unauthenticated shape of req.body need review

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new webhook API route (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) that authenticates solely via `req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not set (i.e., `undefined`), then a request with no header will also yield `undefined`, making the comparison false and allowing the request through (effectively unauthenticated). This is a concrete security flaw in the diff. The body shape itself is validated with zod, but the authentication check as implemented can be bypassed when the secret is unset/misconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Suspicious schema construction in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: [z.string().toString()] used as a computed key does not implement the intended 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(), })`. Those computed keys are evaluated immediately to string literals (likely "[object Object]") rather than creating an index signature like “any string key”. Zod object shapes require concrete string keys; this does not implement “any property with a number is the expiry” and will not validate arbitrary numeric fields (e.g. `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) as intended. The correct approach would be `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).catchall(z.unknown())` plus refinements, or a `z.record(...)`/`passthrough()` pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of .data, and Google CalendarService persists it directly, so every Google token refresh rewrites Credential.key to a Zod envelope without access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, silently corrupting all Google Calendar credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credentials are persisted as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That means `Credential.key` will be written as the Zod envelope object instead of the expected token payload shape (access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date at the top level). adjudication_records.issue_text: The app-credential sync endpoint performs a blind full-object overwrite of Credential.key with no export/backup of the prior value and no dual-write, destroying the user's only working credential copy if the sync payload is bad

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, when an existing credential is found it is updated with `data: { key: keys }`, where `keys` comes from `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))`. This is a full replacement of `Credential.key` with whatever object was provided, with no merge, no per-app schema validation of the decrypted object, and no preservation of the previous `key` value. Therefore, if the webhook sends malformed/incomplete-but-JSON-parsable keys (or decrypts to the wrong payload), the user’s previously working credential data would be overwritten and lost in-place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: symmetricDecrypt in app-credential.ts is called with process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '' instead of failing closed on a missing encryption key

adjudication.rationale: In the new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, the decryption key is taken as `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` when calling `symmetricDecrypt(...)`. That means if the env var is missing/empty, the code will still attempt to decrypt using an empty-string key rather than rejecting the request/configuration. There is no prior guard that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set, so this does not “fail closed” on missing encryption key as the comment implies it should (and may lead to incorrect decryption/500s or weakening security if an empty key is ever accepted).
